fixture_notes: One employee has two present skill properties and two absent properties. JSON_TABLE null extension and UNION ALL normalization remain observable with the smallest retained object.
determinism_notes: Fixed employee ID, JSON properties, skill years, UNION ALL branches, and null filtering; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE mini_skill_employees (employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY, skills JSON NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH employee_skills AS (SELECT e.employee_id, jt.spark_year, jt.java_year, jt.python_year, jt.azure_year FROM mini_skill_employees AS e, JSON_TABLE(e.skills, '$' COLUMNS (spark_year INT PATH '$.Spark', java_year INT PATH '$.Java', python_year INT PATH '$.Python', azure_year INT PATH '$.Azure')) AS jt), normalized_skills AS (SELECT employee_id, 'Spark' AS technology, spark_year AS release_year FROM employee_skills UNION ALL SELECT employee_id, 'Java' AS technology, java_year AS release_year FROM employee_skills UNION ALL SELECT employee_id, 'Python' AS technology, python_year AS release_year FROM employee_skills UNION ALL SELECT employee_id, 'Azure' AS technology, azure_year AS release_year FROM employee_skills) SELECT employee_id, technology, release_year FROM normalized_skills WHERE release_year IS NOT NULL ORDER BY employee_id, technology
